claim: behaviorMate has been used for head-fixed mouse navigation experiments combined with two-photon microscopy.
source: In our experimental setups, we use behaviorMate to combine in vivo head-fixed mouse navigation experiments with 2p microscopy, focusing on one-dimensional (1D) spatial navigation tasks (Figure 3).
evidence: The manuscript describes the experimental application of the system.

claim: behaviorMate has been used for head-fixed trace fear conditioning tasks.

claim: Many spatial representations observed in freely moving animals are conserved in head-restrained animal setups.

claim: Place cells have been observed in CA1 in both treadmill belt systems and visual VR systems.
source: Observations within the medial temporal lobe, focused on all subregions of the hippocampus as well as the entorhinal cortex, have shown that prominent neural correlates of navigation behaviors exist in both the TM belt style systems as well as in the visual only VR systems (Aronov and Tank, 2014; Dombeck et al., 2010; Royer et al., 2012; Danielson et al., 2016).

claim: Grid cell-like tuning has been observed in the medial entorhinal cortex in visual VR systems.

evidence: The manuscript cites published studies supporting this observation.

source: We recorded on average 1533 ± 481 and 1057 ± 169 CA1 neurons in VR and TM, respectively.

claim: VR had significantly fewer CA1 neurons classified as place cells (34.9%) compared to TM (44.9%).
source: Although VR had significantly fewer CA1 neurons being classified as place cells compared to TM (VR: 34.9% (3253/9195), TM: 44.9% (6101/13,454), two sample z-test, z = 14.96, p = 1.27e−50), place cells tiled the entire track in both VR and TM (Figure 5B, Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The manuscript reports statistical analysis comparing place cell proportions between conditions.

claim: Place cells tiled the entire track in both VR and TM environments.
source: Although VR had significantly fewer CA1 neurons being classified as place cells compared to TM (VR: 34.9% (3253/9195), TM: 44.9% (6101/13,454), two sample z-test, z = 14.96, p = 1.27e−50), place cells tiled the entire track in both VR and TM (Figure 5B, Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The manuscript reports observational data from imaging experiments.

claim: There was no significant effect of environment or context on mean ΔF/F amplitude of place cells.
source: There was no significant effect of environment or context on mean ΔF/F amplitude (environment: F(1,5) = 1.9387, p = 0.222, context: F(1,5) = 0.0037, p = 0.9537, Figure 5C, Figure 5—figure supplement 2)
evidence: The manuscript reports statistical analysis results from two-way ANOVA.

claim: There was no significant effect of environment or context on mean ΔF/F frequency of place cells.

claim: There was a significant effect of environment on place cell sensitivity (F(1,5) = 9.85, p = 0.0257).
source: The two-way ANOVA revealed a significant effect of environment on sensitivity (environment: F(1,5) = 9.85, p = 0.0257, context: F(1,5) = 3.34, p = 0.13, Figure 5E, Figure 5—figure supplement 2)
evidence: The manuscript reports statistical analysis results from two-way ANOVA.

source: However, we did not observe any significant effect of environment or context on spatial information (Skaggs and McNaughton, 1998) (environment: F(1,5) = 0.74, p = 0.43, context: F(1,5) = 3.79, p = 0.11, Figure 5G, Figure 5—figure supplement 2).

claim: Place cells in VR have reduced trial-by-trial reliability compared to TM.
source: These results are consistent with previous findings that place cells in VR have reduced trial-by-trial reliability (Ravassard et al., 2013; Aghajan et al., 2015), but still encode spatial information (Dombeck et al., 2010; Aronov and Tank, 2014; Hainmueller and Bartos, 2018; Priestley et al., 2022).
evidence: The manuscript cites published studies supporting this interpretation of their results.

claim: The observed differences in VR and TM place cell properties may result from the absence of proximal visual cues and tactile cues during VR tasks.
source: The observed differences in the properties of VR and TM place cells may be the result of the absence of proximal visual cues and tactile cues (which are speculated to be more salient than visual cues) during VR tasks (Knierim and Rao, 2003; Renaudineau et al., 2007; Sofroniew et al., 2014).
evidence: The manuscript provides an interpretation of results supported by citations to relevant literature.

claim: A subset of place cells changed their place tuning properties when exposed to novel contexts in both VR and TM.
source: As expected, a subset of place cells changed their place tuning properties when exposed to novel contexts (Figure 6A, B).
evidence: The manuscript reports observational data from imaging experiments.

claim: There was no difference in between-context rate map correlation between VR and TM.
source: Moreover, we did not observe differences in the between context rate map correlation between VR and TM, suggesting that remapping happens in both environment types.

source: However, when the decoder trained with familiar trials was tested to decode position in a novel trial, the absolute decoding error was at the chance level (Figure 6C, D) in both VR and TM.

claim: Place cells remap in both VR and TM when exposed to novel context.
source: These suggest that place cells remap in both VR and TM when exposed to novel context.

source: behaviorMate exclusively uses open-source software and is simple to construct with parts that are significantly cheaper.

evidence: The manuscript cites other published systems for comparison.

claim: Head-restrained animal setups pose a fundamental challenge to behavioral research as they limit animals' natural movement through their environments.
source: Many experiments rely on using head-restrained animals to study the neuronal circuits underlying complex behaviors; such immobilization poses a fundamental challenge to behavioral research as it stymies animals' natural movement through their environments.
evidence: The manuscript states a general challenge in the field.

claim: A plethora of treadmill systems have been developed relying on belt-based systems, VR, or augmented reality.
source: In order to address this issue, a plethora of 'treadmill' systems have been developed relying on belt-based systems (Royer et al., 2012; Lovett-Barron et al., 2014; Jordan et al., 2021), VR (Dombeck et al., 2010), or augmented reality (AR), where experimenters move 'spatial' cues to create the illusion of locomotion without actual movement in physical space (Jayakumar et al., 2019).
evidence: The manuscript cites published studies describing various approaches.

claim: VR and AR systems operate under closed-loop control, where the environment responds to the animal's behavior.
source: VR and AR systems operate under closed-loop control, where the environment responds to the animal's behavior (Dombeck and Reiser, 2012).
evidence: The manuscript cites a published study to support this definition.

claim: Olfactory and auditory stimuli have been utilized at regular virtual distance intervals to enrich the VR experience with more salient cues.
source: Normally, these cues are visually displayed on one or more computer monitors, but olfactory and auditory stimuli have also been utilized at regular virtual distance intervals to enrich the experience with more salient cues (Radvansky and Dombeck, 2018; Fischler-Ruiz et al., 2021).
evidence: The manuscript cites published studies describing multi-modal cue presentations.

claim: Place cells, goal-related tuning, and other feature-selective tuning have been observed in CA1 and CA3.
source: In CA1 (Danielson et al., 2017; Zaremba et al., 2017) and CA3 (Terada et al., 2022), place cells, goal-related tuning, and other feature-selective tuning have been observed.
evidence: The manuscript cites published studies supporting these observations.

claim: VR systems have been pivotal for recent findings relating to how cells in CA1 form place fields and mechanisms underlying synaptic plasticity.
source: The increased control over reward distribution and cue manipulation that VR systems afford has been pivotal for recent findings relating to how cells in CA1 form place fields, uncovering novel mechanisms underlying synaptic plasticity (Gonzalez et al., 2023; Bittner et al., 2017; Priestley et al., 2022), demonstrating the power of these systems to test specific theoretical predictions.
evidence: The manuscript cites published studies demonstrating the utility of VR systems.

claim: The behaviorMate UI executes in three distinct phases: setup routine, main event loop, and termination routine.
source: The UI executes in three distinct phases during run-time. First, a setup routine is executed, then the program enters the main event loop, and finally a termination routine is executed when an experiment is completed (Figure 2B).
evidence: The manuscript describes the software architecture and execution flow.

source: Moving the reward location forces animals to learn updates to task rules mid-experiment and has been used to investigate deficits in mouse models of psychiatric disorder (Zaremba et al., 2017) as well as neural circuit analysis of the mechanisms behind reward learning (Kaufman et al., 2020) and the development of signals underpinning spatial navigation (Rolotti et al., 2022b; Terada et al., 2022; Danielson et al., 2016).

claim: Coupling of navigational cues with stimulation in hippocampal CA1 was used for the first successful optical induction of place fields.

claim: The use of VR cues has become increasingly popular in neuroscience.

claim: Different VR implementations have been described previously.
source: Although different VR implementations have been described, for this manuscript, VR is defined as closed-loop control from the behaviorMate UI that integrates position updates virtually and advances cues past the animal to create the illusion of movement, unlike a belt which physically moves past the animal. Various systems for accomplishing this have been proposed and implemented previously (Dombeck et al., 2010; Harvey et al., 2012; Sheffield et al., 2017; Hainmueller and Bartos, 2018; Campbell et al., 2018; Arriaga and Han, 2017; Arriaga and Han, 2019; Dudok et al., 2021a).

claim: Mice can learn to use VR cues as landmarks for traversing environments to specific locations.
source: Mice can learn to use VR cues as landmarks for traversing environments to specific locations.
evidence: The manuscript makes a general statement about mouse behavior in VR.

claim: Neuronal circuits involved in navigation in freely moving mice are similarly engaged during VR tasks.
source: Neuronal circuits thought to be involved in navigation in freely moving mice have been shown to be similarly engaged during the described VR tasks (Dombeck and Reiser, 2012; Dombeck et al., 2010; Aronov and Tank, 2014).
evidence: The manuscript cites published studies supporting this claim.

claim: behaviorMate incorporates visual VR displays into its architecture for 1D navigation with minimal computational load for each additional display.
source: behaviorMate represents a novel contribution in that it incorporates visual VR displays into its architecture for 1D navigation and is designed to adapt seamlessly to novel arrangements of VR displays with minimal computational load for each additional display (Priestley et al., 2022; Bowler and Losonczy, 2023).
evidence: The manuscript cites published studies demonstrating this capability.

claim: VRMate achieves scalability by rendering scenes on separate Android devices, one per display.
source: This is achieved by rendering the virtual environments on separate Android devices (one per display) with a separate application (VRMate). Since the same behaviorMate UI is used for TM and VR experiments, all of the experimental paradigms described in the TM section can be implemented in the VR system with minimal changes to the settings file.
evidence: The manuscript describes the technical approach to achieving scalability.

claim: VR permits rapid visual context switches and the addition of novel virtual objects in a familiar scene.
source: Additionally, VR permits rapid visual context switches and the addition of novel virtual objects in a familiar scene.
evidence: The manuscript describes capabilities of the VR system.

claim: Hybrid setups combining visual displays with physical treadmills are supported by behaviorMate.
source: Furthermore, 'hybrid' setups are also supported in which visual displays can be added to physical TMs in order to combine both tactile and visual cues.
evidence: The manuscript describes the flexibility of the system to combine different modalities.

claim: VRMate listens for incoming UDP packets carrying position updates from the behaviorMate UI.
source: VRMate is a program developed using the Unity(TM) game engine and written in C#; it listens for incoming UDP packets carrying position updates from the behaviorMate UI.
evidence: The manuscript describes the communication protocol between VRMate and behaviorMate.

claim: Each display-ODROID pair runs an instance of VRMate, which renders scenes independently.
source: Each display–ODROID pair runs an instance of the VRMate program, which means scene rendering is done independently by dedicated hardware for each monitor.
evidence: The manuscript describes the distributed rendering architecture.

claim: The distributed rendering approach allows for scalability to any number of additional displays without compromising frame rate or resolution.
source: This allows for scalability to any number of additional displays without compromising frame rate or resolution.
evidence: The manuscript describes the performance benefit of the distributed architecture.

claim: Unity is platform independent, so VRMate can be built for Windows, OSX, and other systems.
source: Notably, Unity is platform independent, so VRMate can be built for Windows, OSX, and other systems.
evidence: The manuscript describes the cross-platform capability of the VR software.

claim: Unity supports the implementation of custom shader programs which can be enabled through the UI.
source: Specifically for researchers conducting imaging experiments, Unity supports the implementation of custom 'shader programs' which can be enabled through the UI.
evidence: The manuscript describes a feature of Unity relevant to imaging experiments.

claim: Custom shaders allow removal of particular color emissions from visual scenes to minimize artifacts in fluorescent protein imaging.
source: Implementing custom shaders allows you to edit color-pixel values in the visual scenes just prior to when they are rendered. For example, this means it is possible to remove a particular color emission from the scenes or display with just a single color (Figure 4G). This is particularly useful for experiments where green or red fluorescent proteins are used to indicate neuronal activity. In this case, rendering scenes with the green or red component of each pixel set to 0 minimizes the risk of artifacts in the recorded data.
evidence: The manuscript describes a feature and its application to imaging experiments.

claim: Separating task logic from VR display modules makes the system more modular and easier to test and debug.
source: Moreover, the overall system becomes more modular and easier to test and debug especially when designing multiple different behavioral paradigms.
evidence: The manuscript explains the software engineering benefit of the modular architecture.

claim: behaviorMate does not require understanding Object-Oriented Programming and C# because it uses configuration files.
source: Third, implementing task logic in Unity would require understanding Object-Oriented Programming and C# (or learning some other 3D development platform) which is not always accessible to researchers that are typically more familiar with scripting in Python and Matlab. behaviorMate does not necessitate programming because it uses configuration files that can be modified in a standard text editor.
evidence: The manuscript explains the accessibility advantage of the configuration-based approach.

claim: The mouse is positioned 5 inches above the bottom edge of each monitor to align visual stimulus to the animal's field of view.
source: Since mice primarily have a visual field-oriented overhead (Dräger and Olsen, 1980), the mouse is positioned 5 inches above the bottom edge of each monitor in order to align the visual stimulus to the animal's field of view.
evidence: The manuscript cites a published study about mouse vision to justify the positioning.

claim: A wireless, tablet-based VR setup is used when the standard 5 monitor setup will not fit due to space constraints.
source: In cases when the standard 5 monitor setup will not fit due to space constraints, we use a wireless, tablet-based setup (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The manuscript describes an alternative configuration for space-constrained setups.

claim: The tablet system consists of 5 Fire HD 10 tablets with specific technical specifications.
source: Our tablet system consists of 5 'Fire HD 10' (2019, 9th Gen), 10.1 inch tablets with a screen resolution of 1920 × 1200 IPS while running Android 9. Additional specs include 2 GB RAM, 4xARM Cortex-A73 (2.0 GHZ) and 4xARM Cortex-A53 (2.0 GHz) processors, and an ARM Mali-G72 MP3 GPU.
evidence: The manuscript provides detailed hardware specifications for the tablet-based system.

claim: Tablets may be connected to the behaviorMate intranet using a wireless router.
source: Tablets may be connected to the behaviorMate intranet using a wireless router.
evidence: The manuscript describes the networking approach for the tablet-based system.

claim: Each device on the network is assigned a unique static IP address by configuring IP tables on the Wi-Fi router.
source: Each device on the network is assigned a unique static IP address by configuring the IP tables on the Wi-Fi-enabled router to bind each tablet's IP address to its MAC address.
evidence: The manuscript describes the network configuration method.

claim: The running wheel design used is lightweight and optimized to have low rotational momentum.
source: The running wheel design used in our setup, as described previously by Warren et al., 2021 is lightweight and optimized to have low rotational momentum.
evidence: The manuscript cites a published study describing the running wheel design.

claim: The lightweight running wheel provides animals with a natural feeling of running while minimizing effort required to traverse virtual environments.
source: This provides animals with a natural feeling of running while minimizing the effort required to traverse the virtual environments.
evidence: The manuscript explains the functional benefit of the running wheel design.

claim: Head restraining bars for mice presented with visual cues are designed to assist with blocking light during imaging.
source: The head restraining bars for mice presented with visual cues (Figure 4H, I) are designed to assist with blocking light that may otherwise be detected during imaging.
evidence: The manuscript describes the design purpose of the head restraining bars.

claim: Head restraining bars can be 3D printed from titanium and reused between animals if properly cleaned and sterilized.
source: These can be 3D printed from titanium and reused between animals if properly cleaned and sterilized.
evidence: The manuscript describes the fabrication and reuse of head restraining bars.

claim: A modified running wheel design with goniometers is required to tilt both implant holders and the entire wheel along roll and pitch axes.
source: In some cases, a modified running wheel design with goniometers is required to tilt both the implant holders and the entire wheel along the roll and pitch axes (Figure 4B).
evidence: The manuscript describes an alternative configuration for specific imaging requirements.

claim: Goniometers are used to align the imaging plane to maximize field of view or level the glass coverslip.
source: For head-fixed 2p imaging, this is used to align the imaging plane to maximize the size of the field of view or, as needed, level the glass coverslip placed over the brain (which minimizes the amount of the material the beam must travel through and maximizes image clarity).
evidence: The manuscript explains the purpose of goniometers in imaging experiments.

claim: VR experiments have been used to examine the effect of rapid within-session context changes.
source: While the introduction of a purely visual VR option for behaviorMate represents one of the newest updates to the setup, studies have already been published that specifically leverage this capability, primarily to examine the effect of rapid within-session context changes (Priestley et al., 2022; Bowler and Losonczy, 2023).
evidence: The manuscript cites published studies demonstrating specific applications of the VR system.

claim: VR experiments have been useful for investigating mechanisms of synaptic plasticity by capturing animals' first exposure to an environment.
source: VR experiments have the ability to transport animals to completely novel scenes which has been useful for investigating the mechanisms of synaptic plasticity, since it is possible to capture the animals first exposure to an environment in a controlled way (Priestley et al., 2022).
evidence: The manuscript cites a published study demonstrating this application.

claim: The VR system allows for simultaneous delivery of multi-modal stimuli such as audio and visual.
source: The system further allows for simultaneous delivery of multi-modal stimuli simultaneously such as audio and visual.
evidence: The manuscript describes a capability of the VR system.

claim: behaviorMate comprises an adaptable framework for probing the function of navigational circuits and the relationship between goal and context representations.
source: Thus, our system comprises an adaptable framework for probing the function of navigational circuits in the brain and the relationship between goal and context representations (Bowler and Losonczy, 2023).
evidence: The manuscript cites a published study demonstrating this application.

claim: Calcium signals were processed with Suite2p for motion correction, cell segmentation, and fluorescent signal extraction.
source: Calcium signals were processed with Suite2p for motion correction, cell segmentation, and fluorescent signal and neuropil extraction (Pachitariu et al., 2017).
evidence: The manuscript cites the software tool used for calcium imaging analysis.

claim: OASIS was used to estimate spike events from ΔF/F signals.
source: Extracted raw fluorescent signals were corrected for neuropil contamination, and resulting ΔF/F was used to estimate spike events using OASIS (Friedrich et al., 2017).
evidence: The manuscript cites the software tool used for spike inference.

claim: A median filter was applied to binarize spike amplitudes into bins of position.
source: A median filter was applied to binarize spike amplitudes into bins of position, and all subsequent analyses used this binarized train as an estimation of each ROIs activity.
evidence: The manuscript describes the data processing method.

claim: All experiments were conducted in accordance with NIH guidelines and with approval from Columbia University IACUC.
source: All experiments were conducted in accordance with the NIH guidelines and with the approval of the Columbia University Institutional Animal Care and Use Committee (Protocol #AC-AABF6554).
evidence: The manuscript states the ethical approval for animal experiments.

claim: Five mice were Unc5b crossed with C57Bl/6, and one mouse was VGAT-cre crossed with Ai9.
source: Five mice were Unc5b crossed with C57Bl/6, and one mouse was VGAT-cre crossed with Ai9 (Jackson Laboratory).
evidence: The manuscript describes the mouse strains used in experiments.

claim: Animals were allowed to recover for 7 days after the injection surgery before cortical aspiration.
source: Animals were allowed to recover from the injection surgery for 7 days, and the cortex lying above CA1 was aspirated to implant a glass cannula to enable optical access to CA1.
evidence: The manuscript describes the surgical timeline.

claim: A titanium headpost was cemented to the skull using dental cement to head-fix animals for 2p imaging.
source: Finally, a titanium headpost was cemented to the skull using dental cement to head-fix animals for 2p functional imaging.
evidence: The manuscript describes the surgical procedure for head fixation.

claim: Analgesics were provided prior to and after surgeries for up to 3 days.
source: Analgesics were provided as per Columbia University Institutional Animal Care and Use Committee prior and after the surgeries for up to 3 days.
evidence: The manuscript describes the post-surgical care protocol.

claim: Animals were habituated to head fixation in a VR environment for 15 minutes after recovering from surgeries.
source: After recovering from surgeries, animals were habituated to head fixation in a VR environment for 15 min.
evidence: The manuscript describes the behavioral training protocol.

claim: 5% sucrose was given at random locations to motivate animals to run in VR or TM.
source: Subsequently, animals were trained to run on a lightweight wheel, and 5% sucrose was given at random locations to motivate animals' to run in the VR or TM.
evidence: The manuscript describes the training procedure.

claim: When animals reliably ran at least 60 laps in VR or 30 laps in TM, the reward was fixed to one or two locations.
source: When animals reliably ran at least 60 laps in VR, or 30 laps in TM, the reward was fixed to either one or two locations.
evidence: The manuscript describes the training criterion and subsequent experimental protocol.

claim: A 3-meter VR track was used for all animals except jy030, which had a 4-meter VR track.
source: A 3-m VR track was used for all animals except jy030, which had 4-m VR track instead, and 2-m TM belt was used in all animals.
evidence: The manuscript describes the experimental parameters for different animals.

claim: A 2-meter TM belt was used in all animals.
source: A 3-m VR track was used for all animals except jy030, which had 4-m VR track instead, and 2-m TM belt was used in all animals.
evidence: The manuscript describes the experimental parameters.

claim: For VR experiments, animals were imaged for one session with context switch after 30 laps in familiar context.
source: For VR experiments, animals were imaged for one session, and the context switch happened after animals ran 30 laps in familiar context.
evidence: The manuscript describes the experimental protocol for VR imaging.

claim: Animals were required to run at least 30 laps in the novel context during VR experiments.
source: Animals were required to run at least another 30 laps in the novel context.
evidence: The manuscript describes the experimental protocol.

claim: TM imaging was done over 2 days with familiar belt on first day and novel belt on second day.
source: In TM, imaging was done over 2 days (first day: familiar belt, second day: novel belt).
evidence: The manuscript describes the experimental protocol for TM imaging.

claim: The power from the tip of the objective never exceeded 100 mW during imaging.
source: In order to image GCaMP8m signals, 920 nm excitation wavelength was used (Coherent), and the power from the tip of the objective never exceeded 100 mW.
evidence: The manuscript describes the imaging parameters.

claim: GCaMP signals were collected using a GaAsP photomultiplier tube detector following amplification via a custom dual stage preamplifier.
source: GCaMP signals were collected using a GaAsP photomultiplier tube detector (Hamamatsu, 7422P-40) following amplification via a custom dual stage preamplifier (1.4 × 105 dB, Bruker).
evidence: The manuscript describes the imaging hardware and signal processing.

claim: All imaging was performed using 512 × 512 pixels with digital zoom between 1 and 1.4.
source: All imaging was performed using 512 × 512 pixels with digital zoom between 1 and 1.4.
evidence: The manuscript describes the imaging parameters.

claim: SIMA software package was used to organize the imaging dataset.
source: In short, the SIMA software package (Kaifosh et al., 2014) was used to organize the imaging dataset, and the imaging data was processed with Suite2p (Pachitariu et al., 2017) for motion correction, signal/neuropil extraction, and ROI detection.
evidence: The manuscript cites the software tool used for data organization.

claim: Individual ROIs were manually curated using the Suite2p GUI to exclude non-somatic ROIs.
source: Following ROI detection, individual ROIs were manually curated using the Suite2p GUI to exclude non-somatic ROIs.
evidence: The manuscript describes the data curation process.

claim: ΔF/F signals were calculated after subtracting the neuropil and correcting for baseline.
source: ΔF/F signals were calculated after subtracting the neuropil and correcting for baseline.
evidence: The manuscript describes the signal processing method.

claim: All analyses were done using binarized event signals.
source: As previously described, all analyses were done using binarized event signals (Ahmed et al., 2020; Priestley et al., 2022).
evidence: The manuscript cites published studies describing the analysis approach.

claim: Events whose amplitudes were above 4 median absolute deviations of the raw trace were selected for binarization.
source: Briefly, ΔF/F signals were deconvolved using OASIS (Friedrich et al., 2017), and the resulting estimated spike amplitude train was binarized by selecting events whose amplitudes were above 4 median absolute deviations of the raw trace.
evidence: The manuscript describes the threshold used for event detection.

claim: The binarized event trains do not claim to reflect the true spiking activities of individual ROIs.
source: We do not claim that this reflects the true spiking activities of individual ROIs.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly disclaims a strong interpretation of the binarized signals.

claim: Binarized event trains were binned into 4 cm bins and smoothed with a Gaussian filter (SD = 2) to calculate tuning curves.
source: Binarized event trains were binned into 4 cm bins and smoothed with a Gaussian filter (SD = 2) to calculate tuning curves.
evidence: The manuscript describes the spatial binning and smoothing parameters.

claim: Individual ROIs were classified as place cells by identifying bins with activities greater than the 99th percentile of surrogate tuning curves.
source: Individual ROIs were classified as a place cell by identifying bins that have activities greater than the 99th percentile of surrogate tuning curves (Priestley et al., 2022).
evidence: The manuscript cites a published study describing the classification method.

claim: Surrogate average tuning curves were calculated by performing 1000 circular shuffles of occupancy of individual trials.
source: In short, surrogate average tuning curves were calculated by performing 1000 circular shuffles of their occupancy of individual trials.
evidence: The manuscript describes the statistical method for determining significance.

claim: To be classified as a place cell, ROIs needed to have at least 3 consecutive significant bins (12 cm) but less than 25 consecutive bins (100 cm).
source: In order to be classified as a place cell, ROIs needed to have at least 3 consecutive significant bins (12 cm), but less than 25 consecutive bins (100 cm).
evidence: The manuscript describes the spatial extent criteria for place cell classification.

claim: To avoid spurious detection, binarized events must have been detected in at least 50% of trials within significant bins.
source: Moreover, in order to avoid spurious detection of significant bins, binarized events must have been detected in at least 50% of trials within those significant bins.
evidence: The manuscript describes the trial-by-trial consistency criterion for place cell classification.

claim: For mean ΔF/F amplitude and frequency calculations, only bins with 3 standard deviations above the mean were used.
source: For mean ΔF/F amplitude and frequency calculations, only bins with 3 standard deviations above the mean were used.
evidence: The manuscript describes the threshold for including events in the analysis.

claim: Place cell sensitivity represents the proportion of laps that had active events within the significant field.
source: For place cell sensitivity, representing the proportion of laps that had active events within the significant field, the number of laps that had at least one binarized event within the significantly detected fields was divided by the total number of laps.
evidence: The manuscript defines the sensitivity metric.

claim: Place cell specificity was calculated as total number of events within the significant field divided by total number of events within the lap.
source: For place cell specificity, total number of events within the significant field was divided by the total number of events observed within the lap.
evidence: The manuscript defines the specificity metric.

claim: Spatial information was calculated as described by Skaggs and McNaughton, 1998.
source: For spatial information, it was calculated as described previously (Skaggs and McNaughton, 1998).
evidence: The manuscript cites the method for calculating spatial information.

claim: FOVs recorded from TM were matched using CellReg, and spatial mask correlation was used to find the same ROIs.
source: Given that TM imaging happened across 2 days, FOVs recorded from TM were matched using CellReg (Sheintuch et al., 2017), and spatial mask correlation was used to find the same ROIs.
evidence: The manuscript cites the software tool used for cell registration across days.

claim: Results from CellReg were manually curated within the Suite2p GUI.
source: Results were manually curated within the Suite2p GUI.
evidence: The manuscript describes the manual curation step.

claim: Rate map correlation was calculated as the Pearson correlation coefficient between average tuning curves from familiar and novel contexts.
source: To calculate rate map correlation, the Pearson correlation coefficient was computed between average tuning curves from the familiar and novel contexts.
evidence: The manuscript describes the method for calculating rate map correlation.

claim: For TM, the shift that generated the maximum population vector correlation between familiar and novel contexts was calculated to account for place cells anchoring on belt seams.
source: For TM, given that place cells may anchor on seams of the belt, the shift that generated the maximum population vector correlation between familiar and novel contexts was calculated.
evidence: The manuscript describes a correction applied to TM data analysis.

claim: A naive Bayesian classifier was used to decode animals' position on the track.
source: A naive Bayesian classifier was used to decode animals' position on the track (Zhang et al., 1998).
evidence: The manuscript cites the method for position decoding.

claim: Chance level for VR decoding was calculated by randomly shuffling cell labels of the testing set.
source: Chance level for VR was calculated by randomly shuffling cell labels of the testing set.
evidence: The manuscript describes the method for determining chance level performance.

claim: Chance level for TM decoding was determined as track length/4, which is the chance level of a circular environment (50 cm).
source: For TM, a chance level was determined as track length/4, which is a chance level of a circular environment (50 cm).
evidence: The manuscript describes the method for determining chance level performance for TM.

claim: The decoder was trained with n-1 trials and tested on the left out trial.
source: The decoder was trained with n − 1 trials and tested on the left out trial.
evidence: The manuscript describes the cross-validation approach.

claim: To match ROI numbers between VR and TM, 500 ROIs were randomly selected and decoding accuracy was calculated 50 times.
source: To match ROI numbers recorded between VR and TM, 500 ROIs were randomly selected, and the decoding accuracy was calculated 50 times.
evidence: The manuscript describes the subsampling approach to control for cell number differences.

claim: Average absolute decoding accuracy was compared to chance level, and the number of times it was below chance was considered its p value.
source: Average absolute decoding accuracy was compared to the chance level calculated from each iteration, and the number of times that it was below the chance level was considered to be its p value.
evidence: The manuscript describes the statistical testing method for decoding performance.
